newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt/currency market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt/currency market closing report.

text.p: The Swedish debt market firmed on Monday along with foreign markets.
A stronger crown and good Swedish fundamentals also lent support, dealers said.
"It feels strong. Fundamentals speak for Sweden. The inflation looks good," one dealer said.
Yields, however, closed off session lows as profit-taking reduced gains.
Nine-year bond yields have now fallen so much that there are no good historical levels to compare with, dealers said.
"We have to break completely new ground," a dealer said.
The six month T-bill rate fell five basis points to 4.79 percent and the nine year bond yield traded five basis points lower at 7.80 percent.
The 7.70 percent level could be tested for the nine-year bond yield, Swedbank Markets said in a weekly newsletter.

The crown strengthened versus the mark to 4.3905 from 4.4170 late on Friday, levels unseen since July. Dealers said today's strenghtening was due to foreign interest, bond buying, and some commercial interest.
"There are rumours that a hedge fund has bought crowns," a dealer said. -- Stockholm newsroom, +46-8-700 1017
